opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll is within the allowed maximum (write for full-time employees), so I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; write is above the allowed maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: Douglas Salinas (E045) requested write access to Payroll. The security record (Note 2) identifies the employee as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training max out at read and write is above that maximum; contractors can never have admin. Note 1 conflicts by listing the employee as full-time, but given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive/security-verified classification, so the maximum allowed is read, and I grant read.
